title: Quaternion-Averaging-Based Adaptive Complementary Filter for Pedestrian Dead Reckoning With a Foot-Mounted AHRS
summary: Pedestrian Dead Reckoning (PDR) can be applied to indoor navigation systems. GPS suffers from signal degradation due to roofs and high-rise buildings, whereas PDR can estimate positions without being affected by such signal degradation. The accuracy of a foot-mounted AHRS(Attitude and Heading Reference System)-based PDR depends on the accuracy of the attitude estimation algorithm used in the AHRS. In this article, a Quaternion-Averaging-Based Adaptive Complementary Filter (QAACF) for PDR with a foot-mounted AHRS is proposed to improve estimation accuracy while reducing computational cost. QAACF fuses a quaternion derived from angular velocity with quaternions derived from acceleration and magnetic field measurements using Markley's quaternion averaging, which combines two quaternions more rigorously than linear interpolation. In addition, QAACF adaptively adjusts the weights of angular velocity, acceleration, and magnetic field measurements according to gait phases and the level of magnetic disturbances. Experimental results showed that the proposed QAACF achieves low Root Mean Square Errors (RMSEs) compared to existing attitude estimation filters while requiring lower computational cost than Kalman filters.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Quaternion-Averaging-Based Adaptive Complementary Filter (QAACF) for foot-mounted AHRS-based Pedestrian Dead Reckoning (PDR) to improve position estimation accuracy while reducing computational cost compared to existing approaches.
AI.motivation: GPS suffers from signal degradation indoors due to roofs and high-rise buildings, whereas Pedestrian Dead Reckoning (PDR) can estimate positions without GPS. However, the accuracy of foot-mounted AHRS-based PDR depends on the quality of attitude estimation algorithms. The authors aim to develop an attitude estimation filter that achieves higher accuracy than existing methods while maintaining lower computational cost than Kalman filters.
AI.method: The proposed QAACF fuses three sensor sources: (1) a quaternion derived from angular velocity, (2) a quaternion derived from acceleration, and (3) a quaternion derived from magnetic field measurements. The filter employs Markley's quaternion averaging technique to combine these quaternions more rigorously than linear interpolation. Additionally, QAACF adaptively adjusts the weights of the three measurement sources based on gait phases and the level of magnetic disturbances.
AI.result: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed QAACF achieves lower Root Mean Square Errors (RMSEs) compared to existing attitude estimation filters while requiring lower computational cost than Kalman filters.
AI.conclusion: The Quaternion-Averaging-Based Adaptive Complementary Filter effectively improves the accuracy of foot-mounted AHRS-based PDR systems while reducing computational complexity, making it a practical solution for indoor navigation applications.

title: Learning 4D Geometric Priors for Inference-Efficient World Action Models
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) have shown strong potential for robotic manipulation by jointly modeling visual future dynamics and executable action sequences. However, existing video-action co-training methods primarily optimize appearance-oriented video latents, which may insufficiently capture the temporally evolving geometry required for precise manipulation. We propose MECo-WAM, a Multi-Expert Co-Training World Action Model that injects action-relevant 4D geometric priors into video-action representations while preserving the original lightweight inference graph. During training, MECo-WAM combines video and action experts with a lightweight 4D expert supervised by relational targets from a frozen VGGT encoder. Asymmetric expert visibility prevents non-causal shortcuts from auxiliary geometry to action generation. To transfer geometric knowledge into the deployed video-action pathway, we introduce decayed 4D read-mask attention, which provides restricted current-frame geometric guidance early in training and progressively removes this dependency. We further propose action-aware temporal geometric distillation, which aligns within-frame geometric relations and their temporal evolution while emphasizing visual regions most relevant to robot actions. At deployment, all auxiliary 4D components are removed. Experiments on LIBERO (98.2%), RoboTwin 2.0 (92.6%), and challenging real-world manipulation tasks show that MECo-WAM improves manipulation performance without increasing inference cost.

AI.tldr: MECo-WAM introduces 4D geometric priors into World Action Models through multi-expert co-training with decayed attention and temporal geometric distillation, achieving 98.2% and 92.6% accuracy on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks while maintaining lightweight inference.
AI.motivation: Existing video-action co-training methods optimize appearance-oriented video latents that insufficiently capture temporally evolving geometry needed for precise robotic manipulation, particularly in challenging real-world scenarios.
AI.method: MECo-WAM employs multi-expert co-training where video and action experts are supervised by a lightweight 4D expert using frozen VGGT encoder relational targets. Key innovations include asymmetric expert visibility to prevent non-causal shortcuts, decayed 4D read-mask attention that progressively removes geometric dependency during training, and action-aware temporal geometric distillation that aligns within-frame geometry with temporal evolution while emphasizing action-relevant visual regions.
AI.result: MECo-WAM achieves 98.2% accuracy on LIBERO and 92.6% on RoboTwin 2.0, demonstrating superior performance on challenging real-world manipulation tasks while maintaining the original lightweight inference graph without auxiliary components at deployment.
AI.conclusion: MECo-WAM successfully integrates geometric priors into video-action representations without increasing inference cost, showing that precise manipulation performance can be enhanced through careful architectural design and training strategies that transfer geometric knowledge while eliminating auxiliary dependencies.

title: GEM-Occ: From Visual Geometry Evidence to Embodied Semantic Occupancy Memory
summary: Semantic occupancy provides a structured spatial memory for embodied indoor agents by jointly representing occupied regions, observed free space, unknown areas, and object semantics. However, existing indoor occupancy benchmarks and methods mainly focus on single-view prediction or room-level online perception, leaving long-horizon semantic mapping across connected indoor spaces underexplored. We introduce HIOcc, a hierarchical indoor occupancy benchmark that unifies ScanNet, ScanNet++, and Matterport3D under a common sparse semantic occupancy format while preserving their native observation geometries, including perspective RGB-D frames and pano-centric observation groups. HIOcc supports three complementary evaluation regimes: local semantic occupancy prediction, room-level online occupancy mapping, and building-level mapping across connected panoramic environments. We further propose GEM-Occ, a Gaussian Evidence Memory framework for semantic occupancy mapping. Rather than using pointmaps as persistent map states, GEM-Occ treats local visual geometry predictions as transient evidence, converts them into semantic Gaussian occupancy evidence and free-space ray evidence, and fuses them into a persistent hierarchical memory through visibility- and uncertainty-aware causal updates. The memory is organized into local caches, room-level submaps, and a building-level graph, and can be queried at any time through Gaussian-to-occupancy splatting. Experiments on HIOcc show that GEM-Occ improves local occupancy prediction, online map stability, free-space reasoning, revisit consistency, and building-level scalability over prior indoor occupancy and Gaussian-based mapping baselines.

AI.tldr: HIOcc unifies ScanNet, ScanNet++, and Matterport3D into a hierarchical indoor occupancy benchmark with three evaluation regimes (local prediction, room-level mapping, building-level mapping). GEM-Occ uses Gaussian Evidence Memory to treat visual geometry predictions as transient evidence and fuses them into a persistent hierarchical memory through visibility- and uncertainty-aware causal updates.
AI.motivation: Existing indoor occupancy benchmarks and methods mainly focus on single-view prediction or room-level online perception, leaving long-horizon semantic mapping across connected indoor spaces underexplored.
AI.method: HIOcc benchmark unifies multiple datasets under a common sparse semantic occupancy format preserving native observation geometries (perspective RGB-D frames and pano-centric observation groups). GEM-Occ framework treats local visual geometry predictions as transient evidence, converts them into semantic Gaussian occupancy evidence and free-space ray evidence, and fuses them into a persistent hierarchical memory (local caches, room-level submaps, building-level graph) through visibility- and uncertainty-aware causal updates.
AI.result: GEM-Occ improves local occupancy prediction, online map stability, free-space reasoning, revisit consistency, and building-level scalability over prior indoor occupancy and Gaussian-based mapping baselines on HIOcc.
AI.conclusion: The proposed hierarchical occupancy benchmark and Gaussian Evidence Memory framework effectively enable long-horizon semantic mapping across connected indoor spaces, demonstrating significant improvements in mapping capabilities across different evaluation regimes.

title: Procedural Volumetric Modeling of Plant Branching Structures for Finite Element Analysis
summary: Precision agriculture, smart breeding, and agricultural robotics require accurate and automated plant modeling. These models provide high-fidelity three-dimensional (3D) representations of plant architecture. They provide the geometric foundation for simulations of water and nutrient transport, light interception, structural loading, and crop lodging. Unlike static plant modeling pipelines, procedural modeling frameworks not only generate accurate 3D plant geometries but also support the generative modeling of crop diversity and the dynamic modeling of plant growth. While terrestrial laser scanning, LiDAR, photogrammetry, and neural reconstruction-based approaches have made 3D plant reconstruction possible, the resulting data are typically in the form of point clouds, which cannot be directly utilized for high-fidelity simulations. We present an automated volumetric procedural modeling framework for plant branching structures that generates analysis-suitable hexahedral meshes from input skeletons or 3D point clouds. The input skeleton is first converted into a rooted graph representation that captures the plant branching topology. Each graph edge is then represented by a smooth centerline B-spline curve, around which a cylindrical tensor-product B-spline volume is constructed. At each junction, incident B-spline volume control lattices are joined using blending operations. The resulting volumetric parameterization is evaluated to generate a smooth and conforming hexahedral mesh of the whole plant. We demonstrate the framework on three diverse plant datasets, namely mung bean, tomato, and walnut trees, generating meshes with both uniform and spatially varying branch radii. The framework also supports dynamic mesh generation suitable for modeling plant growth by locally updating newly added branches without reconstructing the full plant geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an automated volumetric procedural modeling framework that generates analysis-suitable hexahedral meshes from plant input skeletons or 3D point clouds, enabling high-fidelity 3D plant modeling for agricultural applications.
AI.motivation: Precision agriculture, smart breeding, and agricultural robotics require accurate and automated plant modeling with high-fidelity 3D representations. Unlike static plant modeling pipelines, procedural modeling frameworks are needed to support generative modeling of crop diversity and dynamic modeling of plant growth. Existing reconstruction approaches (laser scanning, LiDAR, photogrammetry, neural reconstruction) typically produce point clouds that cannot be directly utilized for high-fidelity simulations.
AI.method: The framework consists of five key steps: (1) Converting input skeletons to rooted graph representations capturing plant branching topology; (2) Representing each graph edge as a smooth centerline B-spline curve; (3) Constructing cylindrical tensor-product B-spline volumes around each curve; (4) Joining incident B-spline volume control lattices at junctions using blending operations; (5) Evaluating the volumetric parameterization to generate smooth, conforming hexahedral meshes. The framework also supports dynamic mesh generation by locally updating newly added branches without full reconstruction.
AI.result: The framework was successfully demonstrated on three diverse plant datasets: mung bean, tomato, and walnut trees, generating meshes with both uniform and spatially varying branch radii. The approach supports dynamic mesh generation suitable for modeling plant growth by allowing local updates to newly added branches.
AI.conclusion: This automated volumetric procedural modeling framework provides a solution for generating high-quality hexahedral meshes from plant skeletons or point clouds, addressing the need for geometry that is directly usable in simulations of water/nutrient transport, light interception, structural loading, and crop lodging. The support for dynamic mesh generation enables modeling of plant growth over time.

title: Dynamic Evaluation of Classical and Control-Aware Optimal Trajectory Planning in Robot Manipulators
comment: Accepted at MERCon 2026. To be presented at MERCon 2026. 7 pages, 7 figures
summary: Trajectory planning strongly influences tracking accuracy, actuator demand, and overall execution behavior in robotic manipulators. Classical planners such as cubic, quintic, and trapezoidal profiles are widely used for their simplicity and smoothness, yet they remain purely kinematic and ignore system dynamics and control effort during trajectory generation. As a result, nominally smooth trajectories can lead to inefficient nonlinear execution and increased corrective control action. This paper presents a control-aware optimal trajectory planning framework that explicitly incorporates manipulator dynamics and actuator effort within a finite-horizon formulation. A midpoint linearization strategy is introduced to improve approximation accuracy for large point-to-point motions. In contrast to prior comparisons, the proposed approach enables fair, isolated evaluation of trajectory generation effects under identical closed-loop nonlinear execution conditions. To this end, a unified evaluation framework is developed in which all planners are executed under identical nonlinear dynamics, controller structure, and actuator constraints. Simulations on a nonlinear simplified UR5 manipulator show that the proposed approach consistently reduces tracking error, corrective torque, and closed-loop execution cost compared to classical methods, achieving substantial reductions in actuator effort and execution cost across all evaluated scenarios, demonstrating that kinematic smoothness alone does not ensure dynamically efficient execution.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a control-aware optimal trajectory planning framework for robotic manipulators that explicitly incorporates dynamics and actuator effort, outperforming classical kinematic planners by significantly reducing tracking error, corrective torque, and execution cost under identical nonlinear closed-loop conditions.
AI.motivation: Classical trajectory planners (cubic, quintic, trapezoidal) are kinematic-only and ignore system dynamics and control effort, leading to inefficient nonlinear execution and increased corrective control actions despite appearing smooth.
AI.method: A control-aware optimal trajectory planning framework with finite-horizon formulation and midpoint linearization strategy is proposed, enabling fair isolated evaluation under identical closed-loop nonlinear execution conditions; all planners are tested under unified evaluation framework with identical dynamics, controller structure, and actuator constraints.
AI.result: Simulations on a nonlinear simplified UR5 manipulator demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently reduces tracking error, corrective torque, and closed-loop execution cost compared to classical methods, achieving substantial reductions in actuator effort and execution cost across all evaluated scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Kinematic smoothness alone does not ensure dynamically efficient execution; explicit incorporation of dynamics and actuator effort in trajectory planning is essential for optimal robotic manipulation performance.

title: SSA-3DGS: Unsupervised Removal of Screen-Space Artifacts for 3D Gaussian Splatting
summary: Novel View Synthesis (NVS) methods, such as 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), rely heavily on the assumption of clean, multi-view consistent, posed input images. Real-world captures can violate this assumption due to screen-space artifacts-static occlusions fixed to the 2D image plane rather than to the 3D world. Common examples include physical sensor defects, environmental obstructions (such as rain or mud on the lens enclosure), capture obstructions (such as a thumb over the camera sensor or a dashboard visible in dashcam footage), and digital overlays (such as watermarks or UI elements). When present, they are erroneously baked into the 3D geometry as "floaters" or near-camera artifacts, degrading the quality of novel-view rendering. In this work, we propose SSA-3DGS, an unsupervised framework that jointly optimizes a 3D scene and a learnable 2D overlay to recover a clean 3D scene and the corrupting artifacts. By exploiting geometric consensus across views, our method effectively disentangles static artifacts from the 3D scene geometry without supervision or manual input. Across diverse synthetic corruptions and a self-captured real-world dataset, SSA-3DGS improves reconstruction fidelity by up to 9 dB PSNR over 3DGS trained on the same corrupted inputs, while faithfully preserving the corrupting artifact.

AI.tldr: SSA-3DGS is an unsupervised framework that jointly optimizes a 3D scene and a learnable 2D overlay to disentangle screen-space artifacts (e.g., sensor defects, obstructions, digital overlays) from clean 3D geometry during novel view synthesis.
AI.motivation: Real-world multi-view captures often contain screen-space artifacts (physical sensor defects, environmental obstructions, capture obstructions, digital overlays) that get erroneously baked into 3D geometry as "floaters" or near-camera artifacts, degrading novel-view rendering quality. Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods rely on clean, multi-view consistent, posed input images, which is violated in practice.
AI.method: SSA-3DGS jointly optimizes a 3D scene representation and a learnable 2D overlay. By exploiting geometric consensus across views, the method disentangles static artifacts from the 3D scene geometry without supervision or manual input. The framework effectively separates corrupting artifacts from the true scene geometry during the optimization process.
AI.result: Across diverse synthetic corruptions and a self-captured real-world dataset, SSA-3DGS improves reconstruction fidelity by up to 9 dB PSNR compared to 3DGS trained on the same corrupted inputs, while faithfully preserving the corrupting artifact.
AI.conclusion: The proposed unsupervised method effectively disentangles screen-space artifacts from 3D geometry, enabling high-quality novel view synthesis from real-world captures that contain various types of screen-space corruption. This approach removes the strict assumption of clean input images required by many 3D reconstruction methods.

title: Decision Protocols in Multi-Agent Large Language Model Conversations
summary: Improving the task performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) is essential, yet scaling these models faces significant challenges such as diminishing returns and high costs. Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) offer a promising solution by distributing tasks among specialized agents to improve the overall task performance. This can reduce training costs at the expense of increased test time due to the discussion and decision-making process. The decision protocol is a critical component of MAS because it specifies how multiple agents collaborate to create a final solution. This thesis introduces the Multi-Agent LLM (MALLM) framework, which implements and evaluates various decision protocols, namely voting, consensus, and judge decision mechanisms, to simulate multi-agent discussions for conversational task solving. Unlike previous work that used a single decision protocol or tested them on limited datasets, this study systematically examines their impact on a diverse set of tasks, ranging from knowledge-based datasets (MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GPQA) and logic-based datasets (StrategyQA, MuSR, Math-lvl-5, SQuAD 2.0). The results indicate that consensus protocols excel in knowledge-intensive domains while voting and judge protocols are more effective for logic-based tasks. Increasing response diversity through independent solution generation improves decision quality, while changes in information access during the decision process have minimal impact.

AI.tldr: The Multi-Agent LLM (MALLM) framework implements and evaluates voting, consensus, and judge decision protocols for multi-agent systems in conversational task solving across diverse knowledge-based and logic-based datasets.
AI.motivation: Scaling LLMs faces challenges like diminishing returns and high costs. Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) offer a solution by distributing tasks among specialized agents, but decision protocols are critical for collaboration and significantly affect test time versus training costs.
AI.method: The MALLM framework implements and systematically evaluates three decision protocols: voting, consensus, and judge decision mechanisms. Testing is conducted on diverse datasets including knowledge-based tasks (MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GPQA) and logic-based tasks (StrategyQA, MuSR, Math-lvl-5, SQuAD 2.0).
AI.result: Consensus protocols excel in knowledge-intensive domains, while voting and judge protocols are more effective for logic-based tasks. Increasing response diversity through independent solution generation improves decision quality, whereas changes in information access during the decision process have minimal impact.
AI.conclusion: This study provides empirical evidence for protocol selection based on task type, offering guidance for implementing effective multi-agent systems that balance task performance with computational efficiency.

title: Physics-Regularized Machine Learning for Proprioceptive Vehicle Localization Using Onboard Sensors
comment: Accepted at the 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS 2026). 8 pages, 4 figures
summary: Accurate and robust localization is essential for autonomous mobility systems in real-world environments. While fusing Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) data with satellite-based correction signals provides precise vehicle pose estimates, performance degrades substantially during outages. Recent studies indicate that Machine Learning (ML) can improve IMU-based proprioceptive localization, highlighting untapped potential for onboard sensors readily available in production vehicles. This paper introduces Physics-Regularized Machine Learning for Localization (PRML2), a hybrid framework that combines the complementary strengths of Kalman filtering and data-driven learning to estimate vehicle pose directly from onboard sensors. A key aspect of PRML2 is its physics-regularized learning, enabled by end-to-end training of an ML model through a differentiable Kalman filter. This improves consistency with vehicle motion models, thereby enhancing both localization accuracy and generalization across driving conditions. We evaluate the performance limits of ML-enhanced onboard odometry on a publicly available dataset and show that PRML2 achieves superior localization accuracy and demonstrates real-time capability. This work also introduces a novel dataset to support vehicle localization research under low-friction conditions. The proposed framework provides a robust and cost-effective solution for vehicle localization under degraded sensing conditions by integrating learning with physics-based priors.

AI.tldr: PRML2 is a hybrid localization framework combining Kalman filtering with machine learning for vehicle pose estimation, using physics-regularized learning via differentiable Kalman filter training to improve accuracy and generalization under degraded sensing conditions.
AI.motivation: Satellite-based corrections plus IMU fusion degrades during outages; ML can enhance onboard proprioceptive localization but lacks consistency with vehicle motion models. A robust, cost-effective solution for vehicle localization under degraded sensing is needed.
AI.method: PRML2 integrates Kalman filtering with data-driven learning, employing physics-regularized learning through end-to-end training of an ML model via a differentiable Kalman filter, enabling consistency with vehicle motion models.
AI.result: Evaluated on a publicly available dataset, PRML2 achieves superior localization accuracy, demonstrates real-time capability, and the authors introduce a novel low-friction dataset for vehicle localization research.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a robust, cost-effective solution for vehicle localization by integrating learning with physics-based priors, improving both accuracy and generalization across diverse driving conditions.

title: Prior-First, Condition-Second: Scalable and Controllable Hand Motion Completion
summary: Synthesizing hand motion that matches the full body motion and the semantic labels is a difficult task due to their high degrees of freedom and the lack of semantic labels. To cope with this issue, we propose a prior-first, condition-second framework for body-conditioned hand motion completion. Our framework first learns a generic body-hand kinematic prior from large-scale unstructured and unlabeled motion data, capturing the intrinsic coordination between global body dynamics and hand articulation. Semantic control is then introduced through lightweight adaptation on top of the frozen prior, avoiding the need to relearn kinematic structure for each control interface. Our framework centers on a streaming, autoregressive body-hand prior that generates coherent, kinematically consistent hand motion from body dynamics in real time, using structured kinematic modeling to maintain mechanical body-hand coupling. To enable practical controllability under limited supervision, we introduce semantically-layered adapters that inject conditioning signals at appropriate kinematic levels, supporting both self-supervised attribute control and weakly supervised text-driven control with only a few hours of labeled data. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our framework improves kinematic plausibility, robustness, and controllability compared to end-to-end conditioned baselines, particularly in low-resource and cross-dataset settings. We further showcase real-time inference and an interactive authoring workflow, highlighting the applicability to production animation pipelines. Homepage: https://AIGAnimation.github.io/HandPrior/

AI.tldr: A prior-first, condition-second framework for body-conditioned hand motion completion that learns a generic body-hand kinematic prior from large-scale unlabeled data, augmented with semantically-layered adapters for controllable synthesis of kinematically consistent hand motions in real-time.
AI.motivation: Synthesizing hand motion that matches full-body motion and semantic labels is challenging due to high degrees of freedom and lack of semantic labels; existing methods struggle with controllability, robustness, and efficiency.
AI.method: A two-stage framework: (1) learns a generic body-hand kinematic prior from large-scale unstructured/unlabeled motion data using a streaming, autoregressive model with structured kinematic modeling; (2) introduces semantically-layered adapters that inject conditioning signals at appropriate kinematic levels, supporting self-supervised attribute control and weakly supervised text-driven control.
AI.result: The framework significantly improves kinematic plausibility, robustness, and controllability compared to end-to-end conditioned baselines, especially in low-resource and cross-dataset settings; enables real-time inference and interactive authoring workflows suitable for production animation pipelines.
AI.conclusion: The proposed prior-first, condition-second approach effectively decouples learning kinematic structure from semantic control, achieving practical controllability with limited supervision while maintaining mechanical body-hand coupling for production-ready hand motion synthesis.

title: Delay-Aware Active Triangulation with Uncertainty-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Counter-UAS
summary: Multi-agent active visual triangulation enables precise 3D localization of aerial targets by coordinating mobile observers with controllable cameras. However, existing methods assume instantaneous state feedback, ignoring cumulative latency from detection, communication, and decision propagation. We present a delay-aware, uncertainty-driven multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for target localization in Counter-UAS applications. Our contributions are: (1) a Dec-POMDP formulation with Age-of-Information (AoI) augmented observations enabling delay-aware coordination -- AoI improves triangulation validity by 10.6 percentage points; (2) a controlled comparison showing that perception-consistent rewards outperform privileged clean-state rewards (0.547 m vs.0.633 m RMSE, 27% fewer track losses) -- both policies are trained through identical observation noise but differ in what they are optimized for, producing a stability-robustness tradeoff; and (3) multi-source analytical covariance propagation incorporating pixel, pose, gimbal, and intrinsics uncertainties -- restricting to angular noise alone causes 2.8-fold RMSE degradation. Experiments with MAPPO in 4096 parallel environments achieve 0.547 +- 0.217 m RMSE with 78.1% triangulation validity, while MLP policies achieve near-zero validity (0.7%), confirming recurrent memory as essential for delay compensation.

AI.tldr: Multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for delay-aware aerial target localization using Dec-POMDP with AoI augmented observations, perception-consistent rewards, and multi-source covariance propagation.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-agent active visual triangulation methods assume instantaneous state feedback, ignoring cumulative latency from detection, communication, and decision propagation that degrades localization performance.
AI.method: A delay-aware, uncertainty-driven multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for Counter-UAS applications featuring: (1) Dec-POMDP formulation with Age-of-Information (AoI) augmented observations for delay-aware coordination; (2) controlled comparison of perception-consistent rewards versus privileged clean-state rewards; (3) multi-source analytical covariance propagation incorporating pixel, pose, gimbal, and intrinsics uncertainties.
AI.result: MAPPO achieves 0.547 ± 0.217 m RMSE with 78.1% triangulation validity. MLP policies achieve near-zero validity (0.7%). Perception-consistent rewards reduce RMSE from 0.633 m to 0.547 m (13.6% improvement) and reduce track losses by 27%. AoI augmentation improves triangulation validity by 10.6 percentage points.
AI.conclusion: Recurrent memory is essential for delay compensation, as MLP policies (without recurrent memory) achieve near-zero validity. The framework demonstrates a stability-robustness tradeoff between perception-consistent and privileged reward strategies, while multi-source covariance propagation (beyond just angular noise) is critical, with angular-only propagation causing 2.8-fold RMSE degradation.

title: Efficient Transfer Learning of Robot Dynamic Models Using Morphological Similarity
comment: Accepted for publication in the 2026 12th International Conference on Control, Decision and Information Technologies (CoDIT)
summary: This study proposes a neural network-based transfer learning framework for modeling the dynamics of soft, fin-actuated underwater robots. We focus on morphologically similar robots that differ in scale and hydrodynamic properties. A model trained on data from a larger robot (source domain) is adapted to a smaller one (target domain) with limited labeled data. To enable label-efficient transfer, we develop an autoencoder-based domain adaptation approach that learns a shared latent representation aligning the dynamics of both robots. Experiments on two real underwater robots show that the proposed method enables accurate state estimation of the body-frame velocities on a target platform without labeled data, highlighting its potential for efficient cross-robot dynamics transfer among morphologically similar platforms.

AI.tldr: A neural network-based transfer learning framework using autoencoder-based domain adaptation to enable accurate state estimation of body-frame velocities for morphologically similar underwater robots with limited labeled data.
AI.motivation: The study focuses on modeling the dynamics of soft, fin-actuated underwater robots that are morphologically similar but differ in scale and hydrodynamic properties. The key challenge is enabling label-efficient transfer of models from larger robots (source domain) to smaller robots (target domain) with limited labeled data available.
AI.method: An autoencoder-based domain adaptation approach is developed to learn a shared latent representation that aligns the dynamics of both the source (larger) and target (smaller) robots. This allows a model trained on data from the larger robot to be adapted to the smaller robot without requiring extensive labeled data for the target domain.
AI.result: Experiments conducted on two real underwater robots demonstrate that the proposed method achieves accurate state estimation of body-frame velocities on the target platform without needing any labeled data from that platform.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach successfully enables efficient cross-robot dynamics transfer among morphologically similar platforms, highlighting its potential for reducing the data requirements when developing models for new robot platforms.

title: WristMimic: Full-Body Humanoid Control with Wrist-Guided Manipulation
summary: Retargeting human object interaction demonstrations to physics based simulation requires reproducing not only body motion but also the object motion and contacts that make manipulation succeed. However, position only hand trajectories do not specify the contact forces needed to manipulate objects, and directly tracking them can overconstrain contact rich finger behavior. We introduce WristMimic, a wrist guided whole body control framework that explicitly separates contact free body motion from contact rich hand manipulation. The contact free body and wrist are guided by kinematic pose targets, whereas the fingers are not directly supervised by human hand pose. Instead, they learn grasping and manipulation behaviors from object tracking and contact outcomes. Our key insight is that the wrist is the natural gate between these two regimes. It is largely free from contact and can be tracked kinematically, yet it determines the global hand configuration and places the fingers within reachable grasp affordances. To ensure reliable wrist placement during interaction, we introduce wrist specific reset constraints and reward prioritization. Experiments show that WristMimic matches or surpasses methods using full finger pose supervision while enabling finger agnostic retargeting across diverse hand embodiments.

AI.tldr: WristMimic is a wrist-guided whole-body control framework that separates contact-free body motion from contact-rich hand manipulation. It uses kinematic pose targets for the body and wrist while allowing fingers to learn grasping behaviors from object tracking and contact outcomes, enabling effective retargeting across diverse hand embodiments.
AI.motivation: Retargeting human interaction demonstrations to physics simulations requires reproducing both body motion and object motion with contacts. Position-only hand trajectories don't specify contact forces and directly tracking them can overconstrain finger behavior in contact-rich manipulation scenarios.
AI.method: The framework introduces a wrist as the natural gate between contact-free body motion and contact-rich hand manipulation. It uses kinematic pose targets to guide contact-free body and wrist motion, while fingers learn grasping and manipulation behaviors from object tracking and contact outcomes. Key innovations include wrist-specific reset constraints and reward prioritization to ensure reliable wrist placement during interaction.
AI.result: Experiments demonstrate that WristMimic matches or surpasses methods using full finger pose supervision while enabling finger-agnostic retargeting across diverse hand embodiments.
AI.conclusion: The wrist-guided approach successfully decouples body and hand control regimes, providing an effective solution for retargeting contact-rich manipulation demonstrations to physics-based simulations without requiring full finger pose supervision.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Velocity Correction for Proprioceptive Vehicle Localization using Evidential Mamba
comment: Accepted at the 2026 International Conference on Indoor Positioning and Indoor Navigation (IPIN 2026), Rome, Italy. 6 pages, 4 figures
summary: Reliable localization in GNSS-denied environments remains a fundamental challenge for intelligent vehicles, as inertial navigation systems accumulate unbounded drift without external correction. Existing approaches provide drift correction through dedicated infrastructure, expensive external sensors, or complex multi-sensor fusion, each introducing practical deployment barriers. We propose Evidential Velocity Correction using Mamba (EVC-Mamba), a learning-based architecture that transforms onboard vehicle sensor data into a virtual velocity sensor for IMU drift correction without additional hardware. A Mamba-based selective state space model captures the temporal dynamics of vehicle motion, while evidential deep learning with a Normal-Inverse-Gamma distribution provides principled uncertainty quantification. The resulting uncertainty-aware velocity estimate is incorporated as a virtual correction measurement into an Error-State Extended Kalman Filter to reduce position drift. Evaluation on real-world vehicle data demonstrates that inertial navigation using the proposed velocity correction achieves localization accuracy within 10% of a dedicated external velocity sensor across different outage durations. The proposed architecture supports real-time onboard deployment at 40 Hz on edge hardware, enabling reliable localization during prolonged GNSS outages.

AI.tldr: EVC-Mamba is a learning-based architecture that transforms onboard vehicle sensor data into a virtual velocity sensor for IMU drift correction without additional hardware, achieving 10% accuracy of dedicated external velocity sensors in GNSS-denied environments at 40 Hz real-time processing.
AI.motivation: GNSS-denied environment localization is challenging because inertial navigation systems accumulate unbounded drift without external correction. Existing approaches (dedicated infrastructure, expensive external sensors, complex multi-sensor fusion) introduce practical deployment barriers that limit real-world adoption.
AI.method: EVC-Mamba combines (1) a Mamba-based selective state space model to capture temporal vehicle motion dynamics, (2) evidential deep learning with Normal-Inverse-Gamma distribution for principled uncertainty quantification, and (3) incorporation of the uncertainty-aware velocity estimate as a virtual correction measurement into an Error-State Extended Kalman Filter.
AI.result: Evaluation on real-world vehicle data demonstrates localization accuracy within 10% of a dedicated external velocity sensor across different outage durations, with real-time onboard deployment capability at 40 Hz on edge hardware.
AI.conclusion: The proposed architecture enables reliable localization during prolonged GNSS outages without additional hardware requirements, overcoming practical deployment barriers of existing approaches.

title: IMR: Iterative Mode-World Weighted Regression for Multi-Agent Trajectory Prediction
summary: Multi-agent motion prediction is essential for automated vehicles to understand the intentions of surrounding vehicles. However, previous prediction-based and anchor-based methods have limitations in mode diversity and prediction accuracy, respectively. These limitations may cause inadequate safety assessments and behavioral deviations in automated vehicles. To address this issue, a mode-world weighted regression loss is proposed to bridge the gap between these features. Specifically, this approach mitigates mode collapse while simultaneously improving world ranking and top-1 confidence. Furthermore, the proposed iterative decoder improves prediction accuracy by recurrently and segmentally generating trajectories. Experimental results show the proposed method ranks first in the Argoverse 2 multi-agent motion forecasting benchmark against other methods.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a mode-world weighted regression loss and an iterative decoder to enhance multi-agent motion prediction for automated vehicles, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the Argoverse 2 benchmark by addressing mode diversity and prediction accuracy simultaneously.
AI.motivation: Multi-agent motion prediction is crucial for automated vehicles to infer surrounding vehicles' intentions. Existing methods suffer from limitations: prediction-based approaches lack mode diversity, while anchor-based methods have lower prediction accuracy. These deficiencies can lead to inadequate safety assessments and behavioral deviations in automated driving systems.
AI.method: Two key components are introduced: (1) A mode-world weighted regression loss that bridges the gap between mode diversity and prediction accuracy, mitigating mode collapse while improving world ranking and top-1 confidence; (2) An iterative decoder that enhances prediction accuracy through recurrent and segmental trajectory generation.
AI.result: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best performance, ranking first in the Argoverse 2 multi-agent motion forecasting benchmark compared to other methods. The approach successfully mitigates mode collapse while simultaneously improving world ranking and top-1 confidence metrics.
AI.conclusion: The proposed mode-world weighted regression loss combined with the iterative decoder effectively addresses the limitations of previous methods by improving both mode diversity and prediction accuracy. This advancement enables more reliable safety assessments and reduces behavioral deviations in automated vehicles, demonstrating the practical value of the approach for real-world autonomous driving applications.

title: Co-STAR: Cognitive Stimulation Therapy by an Autonomous Robot for Dementia -- A One-Week In-Home Study
comment: Accepted for publication at the IEEE RO-MAN Conference 2026
summary: Cognitive therapies have been shown to enhance the quality of life and well-being of people living with dementia (PwDs). However, their use remains limited due to a shortage of trained professionals and the significant time and training required of informal caregivers. To address this gap, we developed and deployed a social robot capable of autonomously delivering cognitive stimulation therapy (CST) in the home. Nine PwDs participated in a one-week ($7$ days) study that involved daily robot-led sessions. Participants engaged positively with the system, completing nearly half of the scheduled sessions, an adherence rate higher than typically observed in caregiver-led CST. Our findings also highlight the crucial role of family members, who often supported session initiation and occasionally joined the activities, enriching the interactions. This work demonstrates the feasibility and potential of socially assistive robots to deliver in-home cognitive therapy, offering a scalable approach to extend access to dementia care.

AI.tldr: A social robot was developed to autonomously deliver cognitive stimulation therapy (CST) to people living with dementia (PwDs), showing high adherence rates and demonstrating the feasibility of using socially assistive robots for home-based cognitive therapy.
AI.motivation: Cognitive therapies enhance quality of life for PwDs but remain limited due to shortage of trained professionals and significant time/training requirements for informal caregivers. This study addresses the gap by developing a social robot for autonomous CST delivery.
AI.method: A social robot capable of autonomously delivering CST was developed and deployed. A one-week (7-day) study was conducted with 9 PwDs who received daily robot-led sessions.
AI.result: Participants engaged positively, completing nearly half of scheduled sessions with higher adherence than typically observed in caregiver-led CST. Family members played a crucial role in session initiation and occasional participation, enriching interactions.
AI.conclusion: Socially assistive robots can feasibly deliver in-home cognitive therapy, offering a scalable approach to extend access to dementia care.

title: Observation Quality Matters: Robust Multi-Fisheye Calibration via Failure-Oriented Analysis
summary: Reliable calibration of multi-fisheye camera systems remains challenging as rig size, camera arrangement diversity, and field of view increase. Existing pipelines can jointly optimize intrinsics, extrinsics, and target poses, but their success still depends heavily on empirical capture rules and the quality of the observations supplied to the solver. This paper studies this dependency through a failure-oriented analysis. We reveal that calibration failures are not sufficiently explained by detector recall loss or global image-plane distribution imbalance. Instead, the dominant failure factor lies in intrinsic initialization: observations with limited radial span couple focal scale with fisheye projection-shape parameters, producing ill-conditioned updates. Guided by this insight, we propose CO-Calib, a plug-in calibration-data construction framework that combines a robust learning-based target detector with an error-analysis-guided frame selector. CO-Calib constructs initialization-friendly anchors, co-visible multi-camera constraints, and coverage-completion frames without changing the existing calibration workflow or optimization backend. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real multi-fisheye systems demonstrate that CO-Calib improves the overall success rate from 68.1% to 99.3%, increases extrinsic accuracy, and augments real-world calibration stability. The source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/HKUST-Aerial-Robotics/CO-Calib.

AI.tldr: CO-Calib improves multi-fisheye camera calibration success rate from 68.1% to 99.3% by addressing intrinsic initialization issues through a data construction framework combining a learning-based target detector with an error-analysis-guided frame selector.
AI.motivation: Multi-fisheye camera calibration is challenging due to increasing rig size, camera arrangement diversity, and field of view. Existing pipelines depend heavily on empirical capture rules and observation quality, with calibration failures not sufficiently explained by detector recall loss or global image-plane distribution imbalance.
AI.method: CO-Calib is a plug-in framework that constructs initialization-friendly anchors, co-visible multi-camera constraints, and coverage-completion frames by combining a robust learning-based target detector with an error-analysis-guided frame selector. It addresses the finding that intrinsic initialization is the dominant failure factor—observations with limited radial span couple focal scale with fisheye projection-shape parameters, producing ill-conditioned updates.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on synthetic and real multi-fisheye systems demonstrate that CO-Calib improves overall success rate from 68.1% to 99.3%, increases extrinsic accuracy, and augments real-world calibration stability.
AI.conclusion: Calibration failures are primarily caused by intrinsic initialization issues rather than detector recall loss or global image-plane distribution imbalance. By constructing better calibration data through CO-Calib's data construction framework, the paper effectively addresses this fundamental problem without changing existing calibration workflows or optimization backends.

title: FORGE: Towards Functional Tool-Use Generalization via Keypoint Trajectory Reasoning
summary: While humans readily repurpose a book, a stone, or a shoe to drive a nail, robots trained on specific tools fail to transfer the same function to novel ones -- a gap we formalize as functional generalization. Such tools share a common functional intent that is visually recognizable, yet this perceptual similarity does not carry over to action space, where each tool demands an entirely different motor pattern. To bridge this gap, we explore intermediate representations including affordance images, human video prompts, and 2D keypoint trajectories, finding that keypoint trajectories best balance functional expressiveness and action groundability. Building on this, we propose FunctiOnal Reasoning and Grounded Execution (FORGE), a two-stage policy that decouples functional reasoning from action execution: predicting generalizable keypoint trajectories from action-free data, then grounding them into robot actions with limited demonstrations. On a seven-tool hitting-function benchmark, FORGE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on unseen tools in both simulation and the real world, achieving over 2X improvement in average success rate.

AI.tldr: FORGE (Functional Reasoning and Grounded Execution) is a two-stage policy that bridges functional generalization gap in robotics by using 2D keypoint trajectories as intermediate representations. It first predicts generalizable trajectories from action-free data, then grounds them into robot actions with limited demonstrations, achieving over 2X success rate improvement on unseen tools.
AI.motivation: Robots trained on specific tools fail to generalize to novel tools despite shared functional intent that is visually recognizable. The key challenge is that perceptual similarity doesn't carry over to the action space, where each tool demands different motor patterns.
AI.method: The authors explore intermediate representations (affordance images, human video prompts, 2D keypoint trajectories) and find keypoint trajectories best balance functional expressiveness and action groundability. FORGE consists of two stages: (1) predicting generalizable keypoint trajectories from action-free data, (2) grounding trajectories into robot actions with limited demonstrations.
AI.result: On a seven-tool hitting-function benchmark, FORGE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on unseen tools in both simulation and the real world, achieving over 2X improvement in average success rate.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling functional reasoning from action execution through keypoint trajectories enables effective functional generalization, allowing robots to transfer tool usage skills to novel tools with limited demonstrations.

title: GraspIT: A Dataset Bridging the Sim-to-Real gap and back for Validated Grasping SE(3) Pose Generation
summary: Robust robotic grasping of novel objects requires datasets that simultaneously provide photorealistic RGB-D observations, physically validated grasp quality annotations, and a principled bridge between simulation and the real world, which existing datasets lack to provide jointly. \textbf{GraspIT} addresses this gap: tabletop scenes in NVIDIA Isaac Sim are annotated via a four-stage physical slip-test on parallel Franka Panda instances, producing trajectory-reachability checks and continuous quality scores beyond force-closure.Of ${\sim}$2.3M candidates, 83% pass as \emph{good} ($s{\geq}0.50$); the 17% that passed force-closure but failed the slip-test provide graded hard negatives. A Real$\leftrightarrow$Sim loop back-projects these labels onto 100 real-world scenes. The release provides ${\sim}$316k annotated RGBD frame sets across 1035 sim and 100 real scenes, with instance masks, 6-DoF poses, physical object properties, and scored 6-DoF grasps. All tools are open-source and Docker-containerized. The trajectory planning within Isaac Sim further allows streaming of high resolution demonstrations for tabletop manipulation policy learning and behavior cloning.

AI.tldr: GraspIT is a dataset that provides photorealistic RGB-D observations, physically validated grasp quality annotations, and a Real↔Sim bridge for robust robotic grasping of novel objects, containing ~316k annotated frame sets across 1035 sim and 100 real scenes with scored 6-DoF grasps.
AI.motivation: Existing datasets lack a combination of photorealistic RGB-D observations, physically validated grasp quality annotations, and a principled bridge between simulation and the real world for robust robotic grasping of novel objects.
AI.method: The authors use NVIDIA Isaac Sim to create tabletop scenes with parallel Franka Panda instances, performing a four-stage physical slip-test to annotate grasp quality. A Real↔Sim loop back-projects these labels onto 100 real-world scenes using Docker-containerized open-source tools.
AI.result: Of ~2.3M candidates, 83% pass as good (s≥0.50), with the remaining 17% providing graded hard negatives. The release provides ~316k annotated RGB-D frame sets across 1035 sim and 100 real scenes, including instance masks, 6-DoF poses, physical object properties, and scored 6-DoF grasps.
AI.conclusion: The GraspIT dataset enables streaming of high-resolution demonstrations for tabletop manipulation policy learning and behavior cloning through its open-source, Docker-containerized tools and principled Real↔Sim bridge.

title: DexTele: A Dual-Arm Dexterous Teleoperation System Based on Motion Retargeting and Adaptive Force Control
summary: In dual-arm dexterous teleoperation, cross-platform generalization of motion retargeting and interactivity of grasping are crucial. However, the heterogeneity of robotic architectures and the wide variety of grasping objects pose significant challenges to achieving precise motion retargeting and compliant grasping in dual-arm dexterous teleoperation. To address these challenges, a dual-arm dexterous teleoperation system (DexTele) is proposed based on motion retargeting and adaptive force control. First, a vision-based motion retargeting module is designed to generate preliminary robot motions from human images. In this module, a motion-graph encoder and latent optimization are proposed for precise and convenient cross-platform motion retargeting. Second, an adaptive grasping module is designed to achieve compliant grasping. This module combines a vision-language model (VLM) with model predictive control (MPC), allowing the system to predict the required grasping force for a target object and perform gradient-based online optimization. Finally, extensive experiments demonstrate that the DexTele achieves precise motion retargeting and compliant grasping with generalization across multiple robot platforms.

AI.tldr: DexTele is a dual-arm dexterous teleoperation system that uses vision-based motion retargeting with motion-graph encoder and latent optimization, combined with an adaptive grasping module that integrates vision-language models with model predictive control to achieve compliant grasping and generalization across robotic platforms.
AI.motivation: Cross-platform motion retargeting and compliant grasping in dual-arm dexterous teleoperation face challenges due to robotic architecture heterogeneity and object variety. Existing solutions struggle with precise retargeting and adaptive force control needed for reliable teleoperation.
AI.method: DexTele comprises two main modules: 1) A vision-based motion retargeting module employing a motion-graph encoder and latent optimization for precise cross-platform motion transfer from human images; 2) An adaptive grasping module fusing vision-language models with model predictive control for force prediction and gradient-based online optimization to achieve compliant grasping.
AI.result: Experiments demonstrate that DexTele achieves precise motion retargeting and compliant grasping capabilities that generalize effectively across multiple robot platforms, overcoming the challenges of architecture heterogeneity and object diversity.
AI.conclusion: The proposed DexTele system successfully addresses the key challenges in dual-arm dexterous teleoperation by combining advanced motion retargeting techniques with adaptive force control, enabling robust cross-platform teleoperation with compliant grasping performance.

title: Intercepting an Agile Target with Net-Carrying Drones using Competitive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: This article presents a solution to intercept an agile drone by a team of agile drone carrying catching nets. We formulate the problem as a competitive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) task. To address the problem of nonstationarity and catastrophic forgetting of agents overfitting to the current opponent strategy, we train the pursuers and the evader using Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) with Prioritized Fictitious Self Play (PFSP). We train the agents in a high-fidelity simulator using low-level control commands, collective thrust and body rates (CTBR), to achieve agile flights for both the pursuers and the evader. We compare the performance of the trained policies in terms of catch rate, time to catch and crash rates, against heuristic baselines and show that our solution outperforms them. Ablation studies show that PFSP lead to more robust policies that can adapt to different opponent strategies, and that a low-level control commands are crucial for learning performing strategies in the pursuit-evasion task. Finally, a qualitative analysis of the learned behaviours highlights the emergence of cooperative tactics among the pursuers.

AI.tldr: A team of agile drones with catching nets intercepts an agile drone via competitive MARL trained with MAPPO+PFSP in a high-fidelity simulator, outperforming baselines and exhibiting emergent cooperative tactics.
AI.motivation: Need to intercept agile drones using catching nets; challenge is nonstationarity and catastrophic forgetting in competitive MARL, requiring robust training methods.
AI.method: Competitive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning task; Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization with Prioritized Fictitious Self Play (MAPPO+PFSP); high-fidelity simulator using low-level control commands (CTBR).
AI.result: Outperforms heuristic baselines in catch rate, time to catch, and crash rates; PFSP improves robustness to opponent strategies; low-level control commands are crucial for learning effective tactics.
AI.conclusion: The solution successfully intercepts agile drones; emergent cooperative tactics among pursuers demonstrate the effectiveness of MAPPO+PFSP for coordinated pursuit-evasion tasks.

title: Imagined Rollouts are Kinematic, Not Dynamic: A Diagnosis of Long-Horizon World-Model Failure
comment: 9 Pages Workshop Paper accepted at RSS Robot World Model Workshop 2026
summary: Long-horizon failure in world models is conventionally attributed to compounding error, a generic framing that does not distinguish what kind of error compounds. We propose a kinematic-vs-dynamic reframing: world models tend to imagine kinematically rather than dynamically. We operationalize this as the imagined Kinematic-Consistency Error, a per-step diagnostic that measures how far a rollout departs from a closed-form kinematic null, paired with a perturbation protocol that tests whether iKCE responds when physical conditions cross a regime boundary. We instantiate the diagnostic on a released DreamerV3 checkpoint trained on DMC walker-walk, where imagined iKCE runs roughly two orders of magnitude above that of matched real-physics rollouts. Across a friction sweep that crosses the gait-collapse boundary, the model's iKCE stays statistically flat even as the trained policy's reward collapses through the same range, providing the kinematic-not-dynamic signature. The diagnostic distinguishes kinematic from dynamic imagination at horizons longer than the embodiment's gait period.

AI.tldr: Long-horizon failure in world models is reframed as kinematic rather than dynamic compounding error; the authors introduce Imagined Kinematic-Consistency Error (iKCE) as a diagnostic revealing that world models imagine kinematically rather than dynamically.
AI.motivation: Conventional explanations attribute long-horizon failure to generic "compounding error" without distinguishing the type; the authors propose a kinematic-vs-dynamic reframing to better understand and diagnose the failure mechanism.
AI.method: The authors operationalize the reframing as Imagined Kinematic-Consistency Error (iKCE), a per-step diagnostic measuring deviation from a closed-form kinematic null, paired with a perturbation protocol testing whether iKCE responds when physical conditions cross regime boundaries.
AI.result: On a DreamerV3 checkpoint for DMC walker-walk, iKCE is roughly two orders of magnitude higher than matched real-physics rollouts; across a friction sweep crossing gait-collapse boundaries, iKCE remains statistically flat while the trained policy's reward collapses through the same range.
AI.conclusion: The iKCE diagnostic successfully distinguishes kinematic from dynamic imagination at horizons longer than the embodiment's gait period, providing a per-step diagnostic tool for analyzing world model failure modes.

title: RoboTALES: Learning Reasoning-Guided Robot Policies via Task-Aligned Simulated Futures
summary: Pretrained video generative models are promising backbones for visuomotor control, but their imagined futures often drift from task intent and are not reliably action-conditional. As a result, these models can be difficult to use for planning or policy extraction. To address these limitations, we propose RoboTALES, a single-stage framework that learns task-aligned simulated futures and uses them to train robot policies. Our approach introduces two key innovations: (1) a hierarchical LLM-based planner that breaks complex tasks into a sequence of subgoals to guide the model's imagination; and (2) a VLM-based critic that evaluates these ``imagined'' futures and uses reward-based feedback to keep the model's internal representations focused on the goal. By anchoring the video generator in abstract reasoning, we produce temporally consistent rollouts and more coherent actions. We evaluate RoboTALES on diverse manipulation tasks from RoboCasa and LIBERO10, and show that our method consistently outperforms existing methods, especially in long-horizon tasks. Our code and models are publicly available at https://github.com/hananshafi/RoboTALES.

AI.tldr: RoboTALES is a single-stage framework that addresses the drift and lack of action-conditionality in pretrained video generative models for visuomotor control by using hierarchical LLM-based planners and VLM-based critics to generate task-aligned simulated futures for robot policy training.
AI.motivation: Pretrained video generative models for visuomotor control suffer from two key limitations: (1) imagined futures drift away from task intent, and (2) they are not reliably action-conditional. These issues make these models difficult to use for planning or policy extraction in robotic manipulation tasks.
AI.method: RoboTALES introduces two key innovations: (1) a hierarchical LLM-based planner that decomposes complex tasks into sequences of subgoals to guide the video generator's imagination; and (2) a VLM-based critic that evaluates "imagined" futures and provides reward-based feedback to keep internal representations focused on the goal. This anchors the video generator in abstract reasoning to produce temporally consistent rollouts and coherent actions.
AI.result: Evaluated on diverse manipulation tasks from RoboCasa and LIBERO10, RoboTALES consistently outperforms existing methods, particularly in long-horizon tasks. The framework successfully generates task-aligned simulated futures that can be used to train effective robot policies.
AI.conclusion: By combining hierarchical LLM-based planning with VLM-based reward feedback, RoboTALES effectively addresses the drift and lack of action-conditionality in pretrained video generators, enabling reliable policy extraction for complex robotic manipulation tasks. The framework demonstrates superior performance especially on long-horizon tasks, and all code and models are publicly available.

title: ThorArena: Benchmarking Humanoid Physical Interaction with Human Motion-Force Demonstrations
summary:
Humanoid robots are increasingly expected to perform contact-rich tasks that require not only accurate whole-body motion but also robust physical interaction with surrounding objects and humans. Although recent advances in humanoid motion imitation and whole-body control have achieved remarkable tracking performance, existing datasets and benchmarks primarily focus on kinematic motion while largely overlooking synchronized interaction forces. As a result, current evaluations fail to capture how external interaction forces affect tracking accuracy, stability, and control robustness.
  In this paper, we present ThorArena, a benchmark for evaluating force-aware humanoid interaction based on human demonstrations with synchronized motion and force measurements. We collect a real-world interaction dataset that simultaneously captures whole-body human motion and forces exerted by both hands across six representative physical interaction tasks. Based on these demonstrations, we propose force-aware evaluation metrics that jointly assess whole-body tracking accuracy, robustness under different force levels, control effort, and episode survival through the Force-Aware Tracking Score (FATS) and complementary diagnostic metrics. We further establish a unified benchmark protocol that replays recorded interaction forces in simulation and provides a standardized evaluation interface for different humanoid control policies.
  Experiments on representative whole-body control policies demonstrate that force-aware evaluation reveals substantial performance differences that remain largely hidden under conventional no-force evaluation. ThorArena provides a practical and reproducible framework for studying force-aware humanoid interaction and offers a new benchmark for evaluating contact-rich humanoid behaviors.

AI.tldr: ThorArena is a benchmark for force-aware humanoid interaction that uses human demonstrations with synchronized motion and force measurements, providing evaluation metrics (FATS) that assess tracking accuracy, robustness, and control effort under external forces, revealing performance differences hidden under conventional no-force evaluation.
AI.motivation: Humanoid robots need to perform contact-rich tasks with robust physical interaction, but existing datasets and benchmarks focus only on kinematic motion and ignore synchronized interaction forces. Current evaluations fail to capture how external forces affect tracking accuracy, stability, and control robustness.
AI.method: Collects real-world dataset capturing whole-body human motion and forces from six physical interaction tasks. Proposes force-aware evaluation metrics (Force-Aware Tracking Score - FATS) that jointly assess tracking accuracy, robustness, control effort, and episode survival. Establishes unified benchmark protocol that replays recorded interaction forces in simulation with standardized evaluation interface.
AI.result: Experiments demonstrate that force-aware evaluation reveals substantial performance differences that remain hidden under conventional no-force evaluation.
AI.conclusion: ThorArena provides a practical and reproducible framework for studying force-aware humanoid interaction and offers a new benchmark for evaluating contact-rich humanoid behaviors.

title: MP-MPPI: A Motion Primitive Guided Sampling-Based Optimizer for Model Predictive Control
summary: This paper proposes a novel method that extends the Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) method with motion primitives for additional structured sampling, which enhances the convergence towards a globally optimal solution. By evaluating motion primitives and perturbed control sequences in a real-time sampling-based optimization loop, this work addresses the limitations of the path planning capabilities of sampling-based controllers. The algorithm is implemented on a quadcopter simulator and tested on an obstacle field navigation task. It is demonstrated that the proposed approach enhances exploration of the control space while maintaining the fast, reactive behavior required for real-time control.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) method by incorporating motion primitives for structured sampling, improving convergence to globally optimal solutions while maintaining real-time control capabilities for quadcopter navigation tasks.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses limitations in path planning capabilities of existing sampling-based controllers, specifically seeking to enhance exploration of the control space while maintaining the fast, reactive behavior required for real-time control applications.
AI.method: The proposed method extends the Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) framework by integrating motion primitives for structured sampling. It evaluates both motion primitives and perturbed control sequences within a real-time sampling-based optimization loop, enabling enhanced exploration of the control space.
AI.result: The algorithm was successfully implemented on a quadcopter simulator and tested on obstacle field navigation tasks. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach enhances exploration of the control space while maintaining the fast, reactive behavior essential for real-time control.
AI.conclusion: The integration of motion primitives into the MPPI framework effectively addresses the path planning limitations of sampling-based controllers, providing improved convergence towards globally optimal solutions without compromising real-time performance requirements.

title: EAGOR: Embodied Reasoning in Omni-direction
summary: Omni-directional (360°) cameras provide embodied agents with a holistic view of their surroundings, making them suited for directional reasoning in tasks such as navigation and object search. Existing Vision Language Models (VLMs) project 360° observations to 2D equirectangular projection (ERP) images and process them using architectures designed for perspective images. However, they ignore the spherical nature of 360° observations, where each pixel represents a viewing direction relative to the agent. Consequently, their direction estimates often become inconsistent under camera view transformations caused by agent motion. This limitation is particularly critical for map-free navigation, where the agent must continuously estimate the target direction in its egocentric frame. We propose EAGOR, a training-free, geometry-aware framework for embodied 360° directional reasoning. Instead of predicting target directions as ERP image coordinates, EAGOR formulates directional reasoning as recursive Bayesian estimation directly on the sphere. It maintains a continuous belief over target directions and propagates it equivariantly under agent motion without training the backbone VLMs. To achieve this, we introduce the Spherical Harmonic Belief Field (SH-BF), whose spherical harmonic representation provides a globally defined, rotation-aware basis for directional estimation on the spherical manifold. This formulation eliminates ERP seam discontinuities, latitude distortions, and interpolation errors. We evaluate EAGOR on two benchmark datasets and real-world experiments with a legged robot across directional reasoning tasks. EAGOR consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving average relative gains of +34.4% and +45.6% on HOS and OSR-Bench, respectively, while improving navigation success by +14.6%, reducing step count by 17.7%, and lowering mean angular error by 24.5%.

AI.tldr: EAGOR is a training-free, geometry-aware framework for embodied 360° directional reasoning that uses spherical harmonic belief fields to maintain rotation-equivariant beliefs over target directions directly on the spherical manifold, eliminating ERP projection artifacts.
AI.motivation: Existing VLMs project 360° observations to 2D equirectangular projection (ERP) images, ignoring the spherical nature of 360° observations. This causes direction estimates to become inconsistent under camera view transformations from agent motion, which is particularly critical for map-free navigation where agents must continuously estimate target directions in their egocentric frame.
AI.method: EAGOR formulates directional reasoning as recursive Bayesian estimation directly on the sphere. It maintains a continuous belief over target directions and propagates it equivariantly under agent motion without training the backbone VLMs. The key innovation is the Spherical Harmonic Belief Field (SH-BF), which provides a globally defined, rotation-aware basis for directional estimation on the spherical manifold, eliminating ERP seam discontinuities, latitude distortions, and interpolation errors.
AI.result: On two benchmark datasets (HOS and OSR-Bench), EAGOR achieves average relative gains of +34.4% and +45.6% respectively. In real-world experiments with a legged robot, it improves navigation success by +14.6%, reduces step count by 17.7%, and lowers mean angular error by 24.5%.
AI.conclusion: By leveraging spherical geometry and spherical harmonic representations, EAGOR effectively addresses the limitations of ERP-based approaches, providing significantly improved directional reasoning capabilities for embodied agents in map-free navigation scenarios.

title: Calf-Integrated Arms for Bimanual Quadruped Loco-Manipulation
summary: Most quadruped loco-manipulation designs trade manipulation capability against stance. A trunk-mounted arm sits high and usually carries a single arm; using the legs as manipulators lifts the manipulating leg off the ground; and even leg-mounted grippers reach two-handed tasks only by rearing onto the hind legs. This paper integrates a manipulator with a prismatic slider, two revolute joints, and a gripper into each front calf of a Unitree Go2. The two arms grasp objects at ground level and manipulate with both hands while all four feet stay planted, without rearing. With one arm carrying, the base stays free to walk. A vision-language model sequences skills from a predefined library at each skill boundary, conditioned on the head-camera image and task state, for long-horizon autonomy. In simulation, the design performs three bimanual tasks: a long-horizon cabinet task under autonomous skill selection, a cooperative two-handed lift, and an inter-arm handover.

AI.tldr: A novel calf-mounted manipulator design enables bimanual ground-level manipulation with all four feet planted on a quadruped robot, enhanced by a vision-language model for autonomous long-horizon skill sequencing.
AI.motivation: Existing quadruped loco-manipulation designs trade manipulation capability against stance: trunk-mounted arms sit high and carry single arms, leg-mounted grippers require rearing to reach ground-level tasks, and rearing limits free base walking.
AI.method: Integrating a manipulator (prismatic slider, two revolute joints, gripper) into each front calf of a Unitree Go2. A vision-language model sequences skills from a predefined library at skill boundaries, conditioned on head-camera image and task state for long-horizon autonomy.
AI.result: In simulation, the design successfully performs three bimanual tasks: a long-horizon cabinet task with autonomous skill selection, a cooperative two-handed lift, and an inter-arm handover.
AI.conclusion: The calf-mounted manipulator enables bimanual manipulation with all four feet planted and a free base for walking, demonstrating the feasibility of integrated loco-manipulation for long-horizon autonomy through conditioned skill sequencing.

title: APVI-SLAM: Real-Time Acoustic-Pressure-Visual-Inertial Localization and Photorealistic Mapping System in Complex Underwater Environment
summary: Extreme subsea environments often cause severe feature de-gradation and estimator divergence in underwater visual-inertial SLAM. Although sensors like Doppler Velocity Logs (DVL) and pressure gauges provide auxiliary constraints, robust multi-sensor fusion during intermittent visual failure remains challenging. To address this, we present APVI-SLAM, a real-time multi-sensor fusion SLAM system that achieves both accurate underwater localization and photorealistic mapping. Our approach introduces a reliability-aware localization framework that dynamically reweights sensor estimators and employs a sliding-window freezing strategy to recover from tracking failures, substantially enhancing system robustness. Furthermore, for high-fidelity scenes reconstruction, we propose an efficient quadtree-guided mapping module that facilitates incremental water-medium modeling and 3D Gaussian optimization. Recognizing the lack of benchmark for underwater mapping evaluation, we also contribute a coral reef surveying dataset with synchronized multi-modality data. Extensive experiments on public and our proposed benchmarks demonstrate that APVI-SLAM achieves state-of-the-art localization and reconstruction quality at real-time speeds.

AI.tldr: APVI-SLAM is a real-time multi-sensor fusion SLAM system for underwater environments that uses a reliability-aware localization framework with dynamic sensor reweighting and sliding-window freezing to handle intermittent visual failure, combined with quadtree-guided mapping for photorealistic 3D reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Extreme subsea environments cause severe feature degradation and estimator divergence in underwater visual-inertial SLAM. While sensors like Doppler Velocity Logs (DVL) and pressure gauges provide auxiliary constraints, robust multi-sensor fusion during intermittent visual failure remains challenging.
